title: Metrics tiles (mobile) — horizontal carousel/scroll + a11y + fallback notes
content:
Context
- Original discussion happened in #design (thread 1819504321). Maya prototyped an alternate for metric tiles on narrow viewports: instead of collapsing into a vertical stack, tiles become a horizontal swipeable carousel to keep KPIs visible.
- Key concerns raised: keyboard/screen reader discoverability, perf on resize, and a non-JS fallback.

What we are building (updated decision)
- We are NOT shipping an "infinite" carousel.
- We are shipping a horizontally scrollable row (linear) with optional scroll snapping.
  - Rationale: simpler a11y model than a true carousel, avoids iOS rubber-band + sentinel tile issues, and keeps DOM order intact.
- On small screens, the metric grid turns into a single-row horizontal scroller.
- On very small screens, we may show 1.2 tiles (peek) to suggest horizontal scroll.

Responsive behavior
- Breakpoint updated from the early 520px idea to 560px after checking common device widths + our dashboard padding.
- Proposed behavior:
  - >= 561px: normal grid layout (2–4 columns depending on available space).
  - <= 560px: horizontal scroll row.
  - JS disabled: stacks vertically (no horizontal scroll enhancements), ensuring content remains accessible.

Implementation notes (frontend)
- Prefer media-query breakpoints and class toggles; avoid repeated measurement/reflow on resize.
- CSS direction (representative):
  - Use display:flex; overflow-x:auto; gap tokenized spacing; and -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch.
  - Consider scroll-snap-type: x proximity (not mandatory; only if it does not fight with assistive tech).
- Keep DOM order identical to reading order. Avoid cloning tiles.

Accessibility notes (updated)
- Keyboard:
  - ArrowLeft/ArrowRight should move focus between tiles when focus is within the tile list.
  - Do NOT implement a hard focus trap; allow Tab to move out of the region normally.
- Screen readers:
  - Container should be a labeled region (role="region" + aria-label="Pinned metrics" or label tied to heading).
  - Add previous/next buttons that are available to keyboard + screen readers.
    - These can be visually hidden on touch-only layouts, but must remain discoverable via screen reader navigation.
  - Do not use aria-hidden on non-visible tiles if it causes focus confusion; prefer allowing all tiles to be reachable and rely on the scroll container.
    - If we later add virtualization, we must revisit this (virtualization can break SR browsing).
- Reduced motion:
  - Respect prefers-reduced-motion; disable animated scroll-to behavior.

Usability check (quick and informal)
- 3 internal usability sessions (5–10 min each) on staging (Jan 30–31):
  - All 3 users discovered horizontal scroll when a partial next tile was visible ("peek").
  - 2/3 users did not notice scroll when tiles were exactly full-width without peek.
  - Keyboard-only tester preferred explicit Previous/Next controls.
- Result: we will keep a subtle peek + gradient edge affordance and include explicit prev/next controls.

Affordance / visual guidance
- Use gradient edges as an affordance (subtle), plus optional scrollbars on platforms that show them.
- Avoid center-dots/pagination indicators for now (adds complexity; unclear value for a linear scroller).

Empty state copy (updated)
- Earlier suggestion in Slack was: "Pin important metrics to this dashboard — tap the pin icon on any card."
- Updated copy after content review (shorter + avoids device-specific verb):
  - Title: "No pinned metrics"
  - Body: "Pin metrics to this dashboard to see them here. Use the pin on any card."

Touch targets (updated)
- Prototype originally had 36px targets.
- Updated requirement:
  - Minimum 44x44px for pin and overflow actions.
  - Prefer 48x48px when spacing allows (especially for the overflow menu) to reduce mis-taps on smaller devices.

Open questions
- Should we enable scroll snapping by default? (Pros: easier one-tile-at-a-time; Cons: can feel "sticky".)
- Do we need an inline hint on first visit ("Swipe to see more")? Current plan is no, rely on peek + gradient.

Action items (carried forward + updated)
- Maya: finalize Figma with updated breakpoint assumption (<=560px), peek behavior, and 44px/48px targets.
- Adele: implement keyboard navigation + prev/next buttons without focus trap; validate with VoiceOver + NVDA.
- Zach: add perf notes to PR and verify no resize-measure loops.
- Sam: confirm empty-state copy with Content Design and update CONS-2143.

References
- Figma: https://figma.com/file/abc123/metrics-mobile (artboards: carousel-v1, compressed-grid; new: horizontal-scroll-v2)
- Slack thread: #design 1819504321
